newsitem.title: MEXICO: Left-wingers seek probe of Mexico's ex-leader.
newsitem.headline: Left-wingers seek probe of Mexico's ex-leader.

text.p: Mexico's main left-wing opposition party has formally called for former president Carlos Salinas de Gortari and a key aide to be investigated over "multiple crimes" during Salinas's 1988-94 reign.
The Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) presented a writ and supporting evidence to the Attorney General's office on Sunday, PRD legal adviser Samuel del Villar told Reuters on Monday.
A spokesman for the Attorney-General's office said the PRD's request had been passed to prosecutors, who would review the evidence and decide whether to open an investigation.
The PRD tried three times previously to bring charges against Carlos Salinas but prosecutors never took them up.

Del Villar said the PRD wanted prosecutors to investigate Salinas, his former chief of staff Jose Cordoba Montoya and Cordoba's alleged former lover Marcela Bodenstedt, who has been accused of links to drugs traffickers.

Prosecutors investigating the 1994 murder of former ruling party presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio called Cordoba to testify in secret last month but no charges have been brought against him. Cordoba threatened to sue the PRD for libel.

In its demand the PRD accused Salinas -- currently in self-imposed exile in Ireland -- Cordoba and Bodenstedt of crimes including drug trafficking, bank fraud, political murders, electoral fraud, influence peddling, abuse of power and obstruction of justice, Del Villar said.

The accusations were the result of what Del Villar called an exhaustive analysis by the PRD of 14 mysterious tape recordings made in 1992, supposedly by government intelligence services, of conversations by Salinas, Cordoba and Bodenstedt with various third parties.
